A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same GP-EIMS research. Their text, equations, five figures, and Appendices A–E are accessible and matchable despite revised pagination and figure layouts.

before.justification: V1 reports original Bayesian optimization experiments on GP-generated functions and six benchmark functions, with regret curves and uncertainty estimates in Figures 1–5.

after.justification: V3 retains these original experiments and reports additional E3I and JES comparisons in Figures 1–5, including Appendix E.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 and Equations (11)–(13) retain the same procedure: sample one posterior function, maximize it, and use that maximum as the EI reference without rescaling posterior variance.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate SE and Matérn-5/2 GP-generated functions at the same length scales and noise levels, plus Ackley, Hartmann3/4/6, Shekel, and Styblinski–Tang. No dataset, task, or input scenario is added.

E2.justification: V3 adds evaluated E3I and JES baselines throughout Figures 1–5 while retaining all previous comparators. E3I was previously discussed only as related work; directly evaluating this closely related multi-sample EI method substantially strengthens the comparison set.

E3.justification: The evaluation framework is retained: the same input grid, Sobol initialization, regret definitions, iteration budgets, hyperparameter rules, and benchmark refitting every five iterations. The added baselines are evaluated within these existing protocols.

E4.justification: The same noise and length-scale sweeps and Appendix E experiments remain. No distinct new ablation, sensitivity factor, robustness scenario, error analysis, or case study is introduced beyond the added baseline comparisons.

E5.justification: Both versions report means and standard errors over 16 random trials covering initialization, function generation, noise, and algorithm randomness. V3 introduces no new uncertainty-estimation practice or significance test.

E6.justification: Figures 1–5 add complete E3I and JES result series while retaining the existing methods’ results. New findings include E3I’s low cumulative regret but stalled simple regret in some SE settings, JES’s weaker performance at the shorter length scale, and E3I’s strong Shekel performance. These additions materially expand the comparative evidence.

T1.justification: V3 adds k(x,x) ≤ 1 to Lemma 4.2 and Corollary 4.5, corrects Lemma D.2 to E[max f] = −E[min f], and removes the 2ν > d restriction from the surrounding Matérn discussion. The principal theorem bounds and proof constructions remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract and central contribution remain unchanged: GP-EIMS achieves sublinear Bayesian cumulative regret without variance rescaling and performs competitively. The revised introduction and conclusion make the comparison with theoretically guaranteed EI methods more explicit without redefining this contribution.

C2.justification: Section 5 extends the exploration-based interpretations to JES and E3I and explains how repeated evaluation of suboptimal points can combine low cumulative regret with stalled simple regret. V3 also discusses Markov-based high-probability bounds and frames guarantees for MES and E3I as future work; the explicit limitations remain.

D1.justification: Section 5 specifies ten Monte Carlo samples and random Fourier feature posterior sampling for the newly evaluated E3I and JES baselines. GP-EIMS implementation information and code/data access disclosures otherwise remain unchanged.

R1.justification: V3 adds JES references by Hvarfner et al. and Tu et al., Paria et al. on Bayesian optimization, and a separate Vakili et al. simple-regret reference. The extensive positioning against earlier EI regret analyses is retained.

P1.justification: V3 adds localized explanations of acquisition maximization and Bayesian regret, a proof roadmap in Appendix C, and grammatical refinements throughout. The overall section structure and scientific narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: All five figures change from two-row/three-column to larger three-row/two-column displays, with explicit y-axis labels, reorganized legends, revised colors and line styles, and daggers identifying theoretical settings. Captions and placement change substantially. Narrower simple-regret axes also hide some early high values.

improvement.justification: V3 strengthens empirical scrutiny through direct E3I and JES comparisons and improves mathematical precision through the added assumptions and Lemma D.2 correction. The proof roadmap and larger labeled figures improve readability, although narrowed axes obscure some early simple-regret values. These are useful refinements to an otherwise unchanged algorithm, principal regret analysis, and experimental scope.
